This is the part of marketing most people miss. Surface-level ads talk about features, discounts, and hype. Deeper ads understand the person: what they fear, what they want, what they believe about themselves, and the identity they’re trying to move toward.

That’s why emotion matters so much. People don’t just buy a product — they buy relief, confidence, status, safety, belonging, or a better version of themselves.

The key is using that understanding ethically. Good marketing should clarify the real problem and offer a useful solution, not manipulate people into buying junk.
